## MvoxNav Layout Audit

### 1. Nav bar structure (left → right)

**Outer container** (`<header>`):
```
flex items-center justify-between py-2 px-6 border-b-[1.5px] border-ink-2 bg-paper
```
Top-level is `justify-between` splitting two groups:

**Left group** (`div.flex.items-center.gap-4`):
- `<BrandMark size="m" />` (logo link)
- `/` separator
- OrgPicker (3 modes: placeholder text, static chip, interactive picker)

**Right group** (`div.flex.items-center.gap-3.5`):
- When signed in:
  - `div.flex.gap-3` containing 5 tab labels (agenda, library, roster, notices, settings) — each `font-sans text-[11.5px]`; librarian chip is inline inside the library tab label
  - `·` separator span
  - `<AvatarMenu />` — `div.relative.inline-flex` wrapping a 30×30px circle button
- When signed out: single "Sign in" link

**AvatarMenu dropdown panel** (`absolute top-full right-0 mt-1.5 min-w-[200px] z-50`):
- Positioned absolutely relative to its `relative inline-flex` wrapper
- `right-0` anchors to the right edge of the avatar button — fine on desktop, goes off-screen left on narrow viewports (but on mobile the whole nav bar overflows first)

---

### 2. Responsive handling

**None whatsoever.** Not a single `sm:` / `md:` / `lg:` breakpoint class in either file. No hamburger menu, no overflow-x hidden, no scroll container, no `flex-wrap`. The header is a single fixed-width desktop row that will overflow on any viewport narrower than the sum of its content widths.

---

### 3. Why the avatar overflows on narrow viewports

The overflow chain:

1. `<header>` is `flex` with no `min-width: 0` constraint on children and no `overflow: hidden` — it simply expands horizontally beyond the viewport.
2. Left group: BrandMark + `/` + OrgPicker chip. OrgPicker chip has fixed pixel font sizes and no truncation. (This is what #65 tracks — chip gets wide on long locale strings.)
3. Right group: 5 tab labels (`flex gap-3`) all inline, none truncated or hidden. At 11.5px font they each consume ~40–70px depending on locale.
4. No `flex-shrink` or `min-width: 0` anywhere — items refuse to compress.
5. AvatarMenu trigger is the last item in the right group. On a narrow viewport the entire right group pushes right of the screen, taking the avatar with it. The avatar button is reachable only by horizontal scroll (if the browser allows it on the body), or not at all if `overflow-x` is clipped upstream.

**The avatar dropdown (`right-0` absolute) is a secondary concern** — fixing the nav layout is the real fix; the dropdown positioning within its wrapper is fine.

---

### 4. Existing GitHub issues — mobile/responsive

**Issue #65** — "MvoxNav chip width on long locale renderings (narrow viewport)" — OPEN.
- That's the OrgPicker static chip growing wide on long translations. Narrow-viewport nav overflow is listed as the symptom context.
- Directly related: any responsive nav fix will also address #65's root cause.

**No other open issues** about mobile nav, hamburger menu, or responsive layout. No existing issue tracking the avatar-off-screen problem specifically — that's new scope.

---

### Summary for scoping

| Question | Answer |
|---|---|
| Responsive handling today | Zero — no breakpoints, no mobile menu, no wrapping |
| What overflows | The entire right group (5 tabs + separator + avatar) as a unit |
| Avatar dropdown itself | Properly positioned (`right-0`), not the root cause |
| Related open issue | #65 (chip width) — same root, different symptom |
| New issue needed | Yes — "MvoxNav: mobile/responsive layout" covers avatar off-screen |

**Minimal-fix path** (avatar reachable on mobile without hamburger): collapse tab labels to icons or hide them behind a single overflow menu at `< sm`, keep avatar always visible with `ml-auto` or `flex-shrink-0`. Low surgery if tabs become icon-only.

**Proper mobile nav path**: hamburger icon at mobile breakpoint, slide-in drawer or bottom sheet for tabs, avatar stays in header. More work but matches the PaperStack aesthetic potential.

That distinction is yours + PO's call.

[2026-05-31 13:45] Research complete.

## Nav Dropdown Clipping — Root Cause Analysis

Files read: `src/lib/components/MvoxNav.svelte` (post-CHORE-76), `src/routes/+layout.svelte`, `src/app.css`, `src/lib/components/DeskSurface.svelte`.

---

### Q1 — Header position + z-index

**Exact classes on `<header>` (line 79, post-CHORE-76):**
```
flex items-center justify-between py-2 px-6 border-b-[1.5px] border-ink-2 bg-paper overflow-x-hidden
```

- **No `position` utility** — header is `position: static` (browser default).
- **No `z-*` class on the header itself.** `z-50` lives only on the two dropdown panels (`AvatarMenu` panel, `nav-tab-menu` panel).
- A `z-index` on an element with `position: static` is **ignored by the browser** — so even if someone added `z-50` to the header it would do nothing without a position class.

---

### Q2 — Layout sibling / paint order

In `+layout.svelte` (lines 63–75):
```svelte
{#if mounted}
  <MvoxNav ... />
{/if}

{@render children()}
```

- `MvoxNav` (= `<header>`) and `{@render children()}` are **siblings at the top level** — no wrapping element between them and `<body>`.
- `<header>` is `position: static`, so its paint order is strictly source order. It comes **before** `children()` in the DOM.
- The page content (`children()`) paints **on top** of anything that overflows out of a static `<header>`. Any page content that happens to cover that area (even with no explicit `z-index`) will appear above the dropdown panel.
- The landing page root is `<DeskSurface>` → `<div data-desk class="w-full wood-bg">` — no position/z-index, but it fills the full width and starts immediately below the header. If the dropdown extends into that area it paints under the desk div.

---

### Q3 — `overflow-x-hidden` clip (the direct cause of dropdown disappearing)

This is **the primary bug introduced by CHORE-76**.

The header now has `overflow-x-hidden`. Per the CSS overflow specification (CSS Overflow Level 3 §3.2):

> "If an element has `overflow-x` or `overflow-y` set to a non-`visible` value, the other axis that is `visible` is treated as `auto`."

So `overflow-x: hidden` on the `<header>` **forces `overflow-y` to `auto`** (not `visible`). This means the header's box becomes a scroll container for its block axis, and any absolutely-positioned descendant that extends **below** the header box is clipped to the header's paint area.

Both dropdown panels are:
- `absolute top-full` — positioned so their top edge aligns with the header's bottom edge
- They extend **below** the header box by their full panel height

The header's forced `overflow-y: auto` clips everything below the header box boundary — the entire panel disappears.

**This reproduces on both desktop (AvatarMenu) and mobile (nav-tab-menu).** The overflow clip applies regardless of viewport width. So yes, the CHORE-75 avatar menu (which worked before CHORE-76) is also now broken on desktop.

---

### Q4 — Stacking context traps

**In the header and its ancestors:** No `transform`, `filter`, `opacity < 1`, `will-change`, `isolation: isolate`, `contain`, or `backdrop-filter` on `<header>`, `+layout.svelte`'s root, or `app.css` global styles.

**However: `DeskSurface` has `animation` on its `<div>`.**

```css
.wood-bg {
  animation:
    wood-orbit1 8s  linear infinite,
    wood-orbit2 13s linear infinite,
    wood-orbit3 21s linear infinite;
```

Per CSS spec, **`animation` with `will-change: auto` behavior** — specifically, running CSS animations that affect `background` — can trigger GPU compositing, which creates a new stacking context on some browsers. The `@keyframes` here animate custom properties (`--dx1`, etc.) used in `background`, not `transform`, so this is a low-risk / browser-dependent path. Not the primary cause, but worth noting: if the header is promoted to a positioned stacking context (`position: relative; z-index: 1`), this guarantees its dropdown paints above the DeskSurface compositor layer regardless of browser-specific compositing decisions.

**`app.css` global `scrollbar-width: none; -ms-overflow-style: none` applied to `*`** — this forces `overflow: hidden` behaviour on webkit scrollbar display, but does not create stacking contexts.

---

### Q5 — Desktop vs mobile reproducibility

**Introduced by CHORE-76, affects both desktop and mobile.** The `overflow-x-hidden` clip on `<header>` is not breakpoint-gated — it applies at all viewport widths. The CHORE-75 AvatarMenu was working before this commit and will be broken on desktop too as of `da00b06`.

---

### Summary — precise cause chain

| # | Cause | Certainty |
|---|---|---|
| **Primary** | `overflow-x-hidden` on `<header>` forces `overflow-y: auto` per CSS spec → clips `absolute top-full` dropdown panels that extend below the header box | Definitive, spec-mandated |

| **Tertiary** | `DeskSurface` `animation` may create a GPU compositor layer on some browsers → dropdown could still lose z-battle on those even with clip removed | Browser-dependent, low confidence |

**Fix prescription (ACs, not implementation):**
1. Remove `overflow-x-hidden` from `<header>` — it is the clip source. Address the underlying overflow problem with `min-w-0` / `truncate` on content children instead (already partially done in CHORE-76 for org chip).
2. Add `position: relative; z-index: <above page content, e.g. z-10 or z-20>` to `<header>` — this creates a stacking context so the header + all its positioned descendants (including `z-50` panels) paint above sibling page content in a defined, spec-guaranteed way.
3. These two together fix both the clip and the stacking-context race. No changes to the panel or AvatarMenu internals needed.

```

```

### v4E schema properties — edition entity

```
name (string, required)        — e.g. "Bärenreiter BA 5103, vocal score"
edition_type (string, required) — full_score | vocal_score | part | reduction | audio | video | supplementary
arranger (string)              — for arrangements/transcriptions
voicing (string)               — optional override of work.original_voicing

file (file, list)              — S3-backed PDFs / audio / video
external_link (string, list)
work (string, formula)         — denorm of work name
```

### v4E schema properties — copy entity

```
name (string, required)
copy_number (number, required)
barcode (string)
condition (string)             — good | fair | poor | lost
notes (text)
```

### v4E schema properties — lending entity

```
name (formula)                 — "Alice Smith — Copy #3"
copy (ref → copy, required)
member (ref → member, required)
assigned_at (date, required)
assigned_until (date)          — due back
returned_at (date)             — absent = still out
renewed_at (date, list)
notes (text)
```

---

### 2. What mvox fetches today (hydrateLibrary.ts)

**Works fetch** (`props=name,composer,voicing,language,year`):
- Fetches: `name` → `title`, `composer`, `voicing`, `language`, `year`
- NOT fetched: `catalog_id`, `catalog_system`, `original_voicing`, `original_duration`, `original_language`, `genre`, `part_of`

**Editions fetch** (`props=name,year,publisher,license_note`):
- Fetches: `name` → `label`, `year`, `publisher`, `license_note` → `isbn`
- NOT fetched: `edition_type`, `arranger`, `voicing`, `language`, `license`, `acquired_at`, `source`, `cost`, `file`, `external_link`

**Copies and lending: not fetched at all.** No availability data is loaded in the current library hydration. The `Loan`/`Edition.on_loan`/`Edition.overdue` fields in `src/lib/types/library.ts` exist only in the mock data shapes; they have no live Entu fetch behind them.

---

### 3. Mock type shapes vs live shapes

`src/lib/types/library.ts` — the **mock** shapes for the 3 task stacks (Returns/Overdue/Pull). These are richer than the live types:
- `Work`: has `title_alt`, `lang`, `period`, `tags`, `notes`, full `editions[]` with loan counts
- `Edition`: has `voicing`, `total`, `on_loan`, `overdue`, `returned_today`, `loans[]`

These are UI scaffolding only — not backed by Entu fetches.

`src/lib/types/library-entu.ts` — the **live** shapes. `EntuWork` has only: `id`, `libraryId`, `composer`, `title`, `voicing?`, `language?`, `year?`. `EntuEdition` has only: `id`, `workId`, `label`, `year?`, `publisher?`, `isbn?`.

---

### 4. Filter dimension status table

| Filter dimension | v4E schema field | Currently fetched? | Currently in EntuWork/Edition? | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Title search | `work.name` | Yes | Yes (`title`) | Full text search needs client-side filter or API `?name.string=` query |
| Composer | `work.composer` | Yes | Yes | Ready |
| Voicing/scoring | `work.original_voicing` | No — wrong field fetched | Partial: `work.voicing` fetched but this maps to `original_voicing` in schema; `edition.voicing` override NOT fetched | `hydrateLibrary` fetches `props=...voicing...` against work — but v4E field name is `original_voicing` not `voicing`; worth verifying what Entu actually returns |
| Language | `work.original_language` | No — wrong field fetched | Partial: `work.language` fetched but schema field is `original_language`; same name-mismatch risk | List-valued in schema; filter needs multi-value handling |
| Genre | `work.genre` | No | No | In schema, list-valued, not fetched |
| Catalog system (BWV etc.) | `work.catalog_system` + `catalog_id` | No | No | In schema, not fetched |
| Edition type | `edition.edition_type` | No | No | In schema (required!), not fetched |
| Arranger | `edition.arranger` | No | No | In schema, not fetched |
| License status | `edition.license` | No | No | public_domain/licensed/owned — in schema, not fetched |
| Has files (PDF/audio) | `edition.file` | No | No | In schema, not fetched; presence derivable if file list non-empty |
| Availability (on loan / available) | `copy` count vs `lending.returned_at` null | Not fetched | No | Requires fetching copies + open lendings per edition; no existing query |
| Publisher | `edition.publisher` | Yes | Yes | Could filter by publisher |
| Year (work) | `work.original_duration` / no year on work | — | `year` fetched on work | **Note: v4E `work` has no `year` property in schema** — only `original_duration`. The `year` in `EntuWork` may be mapping to nothing or a custom field |
| Year (edition) | `edition.year` | Yes | Yes | Edition publication year — fetched |

---

### 5. Key findings

**Voicing/language name mismatch risk:** `hydrateLibrary` fetches `props=name,composer,voicing,language,year` against work entities. The v4E schema fields are `original_voicing` and `original_language` (not `voicing`/`language`). Whether Entu returns values for a mismatched prop name is untested — these may silently come back empty. Needs a probe or a check against what the polyphony DB actually has in work entities.

**Work year is not a v4E field:** v4E `work` has no `year` property — only `original_duration` (minutes). The `year` currently fetched (`w.year?.[0]?.number`) would return nothing from a v4E-compliant Entu db. Either the real works have a `year` property that's outside schema, or this is dead code.

**Availability requires additional fetches:** copy count per edition (to know total) + open lending count (where `returned_at` is absent) per edition. Two extra queries per edition batch, or one aggregated query. Not currently fetched.

**Genre not fetched — low cost to add:** `genre` is in schema, list-valued, not fetched. Adding `genre` to the works `props=` query is a one-line change in `hydrateLibrary.ts` and one field addition to `EntuWork`. Data population in the Entu db is the unknown.

**Edition type not fetched:** `edition_type` is required in v4E schema — every edition should have it. Not in the current `EntuEdition` type. Adding it is trivial (same one-line props addition). Enables filter by score type (vocal_score, part, audio, etc.).

That breaks AC2 ("the 240px+1fr two-column grid are not rendered; layout is single-column") and the spec's List-mode "Hidden: the two-column grid".

## Session JWT Storage — Ground Truth

Files read: `src/lib/auth/storage.ts`, `src/routes/auth/callback/+page.svelte`, `src/routes/auth/callback/+page.server.ts`, `src/routes/auth/logout/perform-logout.ts`, `src/hooks.server.ts`, plus a grep of all `src/` for `cookie`/`cookies`/`event.locals`.

---

### 1. Where the JWT is stored after login

`src/routes/auth/callback/+page.svelte` (client-side `$effect`, runs in browser):

```ts
setToken(result.token);     // localStorage.setItem('token', token)
setAccounts(result.accounts); // localStorage.setItem('accounts', ...)
setUser(result.user);         // localStorage.setItem('user', ...)
```

**All three writes are to `localStorage`.** No `cookies.set(...)` call anywhere in the auth flow. The callback `+page.server.ts` only validates the `?key=` param and passes the session token down as `data` — it sets no cookies.

---

### 2. `getToken()` — where it reads from

`src/lib/auth/storage.ts:40–46`:

```ts
export function getToken(): string | null {
  if (isStaleVersion()) {
    clearAll({ preserveProvider: false });
    return null;
  }
  return localStorage.getItem(KEYS.token);   // key name: 'token'
}
```

**Pure `localStorage.getItem('token')`.** No cookie read, no server-side origin.

---

### 3. Logout — how state is cleared

`src/routes/auth/logout/perform-logout.ts`:

```ts
export function performLogout(): void {
  clearAll({ preserveProvider: false });
}
```

`clearAll` removes `localStorage` keys `token`, `accounts`, `user`, `mvox.token_version` and clears `sessionStorage`. **No `cookies.delete()` call.** The logout route has no `+page.server.ts` at all.

---

### 4. Cookies — entire codebase

Grep of all `src/**/*.ts` and `src/**/*.svelte` for `cookie`, `cookies`, `event.locals`, `locals.` — **zero hits** (excluding spec files and `.svelte-kit/` generated output).

There are **no cookies anywhere in the mvox codebase** — not set, not read, not deleted.

---

### 5. `hooks.server.ts` / `event.locals`

```ts
export const handle: Handle = async ({ event, resolve }) => {
  return resolve(event);
};
```

`event.locals` is never populated. No session object, no user, no token. The server is completely blind at the hooks level.

---

### 6. Can the server read auth state for CHORE-79?

**No.** The server has zero visibility into auth state today:

- No cookie carries the JWT or any session indicator.
- `event.locals` is empty.
- The only auth state is in `localStorage`, which is inaccessible to the server.

---

### Design implications for CHORE-79

| Approach | What's needed |
|---|---|
| **Global server-side redirect** (`hooks.server.ts`) | Requires a cookie the server can read. Needs a new step: after OAuth exchange, mirror the JWT (or a separate session flag) into an httpOnly (or at minimum readable) cookie via a SvelteKit server endpoint. |
| **Per-route server guard** (`+page.server.ts` / `+layout.server.ts`) | Same prerequisite — server still can't see auth without a cookie. |
| **Client-side guard** (`$effect` + `goto`) | Usable today with no infrastructure change. Pattern already exists in `/library`. Downside: page renders before redirect fires (the flash PO wants to eliminate). |
| **Hybrid: cookie flag + server redirect** | On login callback, fire a server endpoint (`/auth/set-session`) that sets a lightweight httpOnly cookie (just a boolean or the token). `hooks.server.ts` reads the cookie to gate protected routes. The full JWT stays in localStorage for Entu API calls. This is the minimal path to true server-side guard. |

**Bottom line for the design conversation with PO:** a true no-flash server-side guard requires introducing a session cookie — that's new infrastructure. The question is whether to do that as part of CHORE-79 or whether a client-side guard (which exists today as a pattern) is acceptable for now.
